name: Fanum tax
blurb: Taking a bite of a friend's food, named after the streamer Fanum
title: Fanum Tax Meaning: What Does Fanum Tax Mean in Slang?
description: Fanum tax means taking a bite of a friend's food. It is named after streamer Fanum, who took Kai Cenat's food on stream; it went viral in 2023.
answer: A Fanum tax is a playful "fee" of food: when a friend grabs a fry, a slice or a bite of your snack, they are Fanum taxing you. The phrase is named after Fanum, a Twitch streamer and member of the AMP group, who kept taking food from other members on stream, especially Kai Cenat. The earliest known clip was posted on 23 December 2022, it took off on TikTok in June 2023, and by late 2023 it was one of the best-known pieces of Gen Alpha slang.

body: The joke treats food-snatching as a tax that friends are entitled to collect. It is used as a verb ("he Fanum taxed my nuggets"), as a noun ("that's the Fanum tax") and as a warning ("hide your chips, Fanum tax incoming"). It is almost always friendly; nobody really means a tax on anything.
Fanum is a real streamer, and the phrase grew out of the AMP crew's streams and clips rather than any official definition.

head: Date
Event
rows: A clip of a Christmas-themed stream, in which Fanum barges in to take Kai Cenat's cookies, is posted on YouTube; it is the earliest known "Fanum tax"
AMP members use the phrase on stream and clips go viral on TikTok; on 24 June Kai Cenat's channel posts a compilation of Fanum taking his food
TikTok users start parodying how often the phrase is used
A parody song pairs it with "Sticking Out Your Gyat for the Rizzler", spawning many remixes
Fanum tax is widely used by Gen Z and Gen Alpha, often ironically

ul: "My little sister Fanum taxed half my pizza."
"Eating in the car so my brother can't charge the Fanum tax."
"Parents Fanum taxing their kids' Halloween candy."
Strings of brainrot slang like "rizz, gyat, Fanum tax, Ohio"

body: The phrase peaked in 2023 and is now a fixed part of Gen Alpha slang, often listed with skibidi, rizz and gyat when adults try to decode kids' talk. It is still the go-to joke whenever someone reaches for another person's food.

faq.a: A Twitch streamer and member of AMP, the streamer group around Kai Cenat. His habit of taking other members' food on stream gave the phrase its name.
No, it is a friendly joke between people who know each other. Actually taking a stranger's food is still rude.
The earliest known clip is from 23 December 2022. It went viral on TikTok in June 2023.
